Senses.Explanation: Like heaven overspreading: the total reach of the one thing — Deshan's stick for one master, the great matter under everyone's heels for another, and the bare answer to a hundred-million Wenshus. Fenyang Shanzhao sets the Song root in verse: true gold from the Li river weighs no more, road gravel no less — heaven overspreading, earth upbearing — and under that roof the utterly poor son comes home while the misjudging crowd quarrels over him; Yuanwu Keqin, at the request of the transport official Liu, works it through the wisdom-light that breaks the dark of birth-and-death and the diamond sword that cuts the fetters: where the break-through happens one thought is not more, and in the use of it the whole body is eye — until it comes to heaven overspreading and earth upbearing, sun shining on all, wind cooling all, not one thread shifted, not one mote screening; Dahui Zonggao diagnoses the racing mind the teaching calls restlessness, and then plants what none of it touches: under each person's heels a stretch of the great matter that neither sinks nor races — like heaven overspreading, like earth upbearing; before there was a world this great matter already was, and when the world breaks, it will not have stirred a hair-tip; Tian'an Sheng, pressed on the one true Wenshu — no second Wenshu, so why a hundred-million Wenshus? — answers with the bare couplet: heaven overspreading, earth upbearing, and when the disciple laughs at Kashyapa's silence he lets the bystanders fall over laughing. Chaozong Tongren, at the evening assembly of Wen-tao hermitage in Shucheng, rules what a lineage master must do: Deshan's stick at the gate is heaven overspreading, Linji's shout at the gate is earth upbearing — never dropping to second or third, never cheating anyone's sons and daughters, while those who guide by capacity have the three vehicles and twelve divisions instead; Daxiu Zhu, watching the gate dwindle, refuses to play teacher for pleasure: a great man standing between heaven and earth must plant his body and walk the way — like heaven overspreading, like earth upbearing — the rain of the teaching falling equal, the three grasses and two trees all moistened; Gusu Zun asks the assembly whether they see it through: this one thing is not less in the commoner nor more in the sage — see straight through and it stands like heaven overspreading and earth upbearing, with no facing or backing, no near and far; Tianyi Juxiang, against branch-chasing after a painted cake, turns it home: the ten thousand things are the light of mind, the conditions announce the nature — know the one mind and the ten thousand things are clear, like heaven overspreading and earth upbearing, sun, moon, and stars, rivers and sacred peaks, down to the whole treasury of forms, all showing forth within it, never lacking one point.
